output.brief: The evidence points mainly to Callerby's own decision, not Halden, as the cause of most of the slip. The tower crane and frame crew moved to the Kestrel job in October 2025, before the CO-09 change order was issued on 6 November. Site staff describe autumn and winter as dead, with steel on the ground. The tamper-proof RFI platform shows the architect answered 62 of 64 queries within the contract period. The two exceptions were late finishes queries that Callerby marked as having no programme impact. Of the 41 RFIs the draft claim calls late, 39 sat in Callerby's own draft status for 9–47 days before submission. So the draft claim's late-information argument is unsound, and it should not go out as drafted. Submitting it risks a misleading claim, and Fenmore is paid a share of anything recovered. CO-09 was a real structural change and may justify some time, but nobody has measured that. I could not confirm whether the incentive scheme drove the crane move. Next steps: hold the 1 December submission, and commission an independent delay analysis, using the crane ledger and site diaries, to see if a narrow CO-09 claim stands. Do not discipline the superintendent. Do not suspend the incentive scheme yet. Confidence is moderate.
